texts: good. the wall is typed as a harbor wall (with "wall" as its genus) and holds a lantern group counted at twenty-four.

good. the boats, the lanterns, the beacon capacity and "at night" are all kept, and the use is recorded both of the boat group and of each individual boat, so a later fact about one boat still connects.
good. "short" and "squat" are each handed to every harbor lantern by their own rule, rather than being pinned on the group as a single object.

bad: in the result clause "a harbor lantern" was pinned to one particular lantern that the parse also asserts to exist outright, so the rule reads "that same single lantern burns its essence every time" instead of "whichever harbor lantern is involved, on each occasion". Use the definite plural, so the lanterns are the ones the world already established: "Whenever wind reflects off the water at the harbor wall, the harbor lanterns burn their mire-essence quickly." If you mean it lantern-by-lantern, put the lantern into the condition instead: "Whenever wind reflects off the water at a harbor lantern, that lantern burns its mire-essence quickly."
good. the bare plural becomes a fireable rule giving every harbor-lantern Keeper a lives-near-the-harbor fact, and the compound kind carries its own keeps-harbor-lanterns atoms.
